bib.title: Enhancing Robustness in Large Language Models: Prompting for Mitigating the Impact of Irrelevant Information

question: Why do LLMs lose reasoning accuracy when a problem contains irrelevant information, and can prompting mitigate it?
hypothesis: LLMs can identify irrelevant information but cannot self-exclude it; explicitly filtering it before reasoning should recover accuracy.
contributions: GSMIR dataset of GSM8K problems with a thematically related irrelevant sentence
Finding that LLMs identify irrelevant information but fail to exclude it
ATF (Analysis to Filtration) prompting, combinable with SP, COT, 0-COT, LTM

method.summary: Builds GSMIR by inserting one irrelevant sentence into 500 GSM8K problems. Tests whether GPT-3.5 models identify and exclude it, then proposes ATF: an LLM-generated analysis demonstration that lists irrelevant clauses, then a filtration prompt that rewrites the question without them, then ordinary prompting on the filtered question.
method.task: grade-school arithmetic reasoning with distractor sentence

datasets.name: GSMIR
datasets.source: 500 random GSM8K problems each with one inserted irrelevant sentence; two types (numerical: ratio, integer, percentage; opinion-based), four templates; released at github.com/ymt9/GSMIR
datasets.preprocessing: irrelevant sentence inserted before the standard problem

datasets.name: GSM8K
datasets.size: 4 items drawn at random as demonstrations

inference.prompting:
10 demonstrations per method (6 from GSMIC, 4 from GSM8K); baselines SP, COT, 0-COT, LTM, IP. ATF demonstration format: [Q: , A: Because , Finally, the answer is ]; test input [, Q:

, A: Because , Finally, ]. Analysis demonstrations are generated by the LLM itself by decomposing q into subclauses and judging each.

other.note: Demonstrations for the identification step come from other datasets than GSMIR.

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of GSMIR or GSM8K-SLC problems answered correctly

metrics.name: identification rate
metrics.definition: correct only if presence of irrelevant info is determined and the irrelevant info correctly pinpointed

eval.protocol: Single reported number per cell; no seeds, no significance test stated.

prompts.text: Q: Does the question contain any irrelevant information? If yes, what is the irrelevant information? A: The answer is
If there is irrelevant information, please exclude it and output the context after excluding the irrelevant information. If there is no irrelevant information, please directly output the context.

results.claim: ATF raises COT accuracy on GSMIR from 50.2 to 74.9 (largest gain)
results.setup: GSMIR (500 GSM8K problems + one irrelevant sentence), GPT-3.5-Turbo, 10 demonstrations

results.claim: Irrelevant sentence drops COT accuracy from 77.8 to 55.2
Irrelevant sentence drops SP accuracy from 29.4 to 18.5
LTM+ATF reaches 69.9, 3.5 points under accuracy on original questions
results.quote: the accuracy significantly increased to 69.9% when applying LTM combined with ATF, only 3.5% lower than its reasoning accuracy on the original questions

results.claim: Share of COT errors caused by irrelevant info where model nonetheless identified the irrelevant info: 70.3%
results.note: 538 exceeds the 500 problems in GSMIR; the counting unit is unexplained

results.claim: Same for SP: 76.3% (232/304) of errors had the irrelevant info identified; models identify but do not exclude it

limits: Only a single irrelevant sentence per problem; authors concede real data has multiple noise items.
Only GPT-3.5-Turbo and 16k; other LLMs left to future work.
Arithmetic word problems only; no decoding settings, temperature or seeds given.
Error counts of 304 and 538 exceed 500 problems, unexplained.
IP does not uniformly lower accuracy despite the text (0-COT+IP 58.9 > 0-COT 52.0).
